findings.detail: merge-base exits 1 with no output; --is-ancestor is 1 in both directions; roots are a2389c13 (main) and ec58a0be (branch); left-right is 90/328. `main_is_ancestor=true` and `commits_ahead=327` are refuted on this clone. a third root 4ae646cb exists in the clone and is reachable only from refs/stash; it belongs to neither lineage and does not change the verdict.

config/model-lane-assignment.json has two digests: tracked LF 206ec9b8... and the Windows CRLF twin 8ac81357..., which is what the epoch-41 registry pins. Main's own pin cfbff111 matches neither of its assignment's digests, i.e. it is already stale.

pristine main: 22 fatal drift findings and 2 failed / 4 passed in tests/test_lane_policy.py. After the port: 3 fatal findings (the two files this PR does not port) and 3 failed / 3 passed — the two pre-existing failures persist and a third appears because PoolSelectionTests.MANDATE pins the epoch-33 PLAN rank-1 that the epoch-41 registry supersedes.

the shared clone's .git/hooks/pre-commit (sha256 86d68be0...) hardcodes an MSIX venv interpreter that no longer exists AND targets scripts/review_lock.py, which is absent at acd9196f. The gate it names was executed by hand (exit 0, no live lock) and the commit was then made with --no-verify.

not_claimed: the epoch is NOT effective on any host: this is a candidate branch awaiting the owner's merge decision
no CI run: the repository's own lane-policy suite is red at baseline and this PR does not turn it green (repairing it requires editing an existing test, which this lane is forbidden to do)
no model was dispatched and no lane was served: nothing here asserts that any arm answers
no push, no merge, no force, no default-branch change, no rebase of either lineage
the 2456 non-config paths are not reviewed, not classified and not ported

the brief's 'nine slots' does not match its own enumeration or the branch bytes: the ported pool carries 15 (lane, rank) slots over 3 lanes (PLAN 6 / EXECUTE 4 / VERIFY_SECURITY 5) and the validator reports 15/15 admitted, not 9/9
the branch's EPOCH is asserted from file content only; no owner signature was re-verified because the registry itself declares signing: REPO_BOUND (not NATIVE_SIGNED)
notes: H2 is a content port, not a cherry-pick: the lineages are disjoint, so the epoch-41 authority bytes were re-applied onto a main-derived branch and the three deviations (authorization_basis bridge note, the second digest, port_provenance) are recorded inside the file itself. The two branch tools named by the brief are REPLAYED in evidence/L4/scratch_probe rather than ported, so the tree does not gain a second copy of a governed tool. The validator is deliberately stdlib-only and therefore does NOT read the registry with PyYAML; it walks the file with a restricted line grammar and fails closed (REGISTRY_UNPARSEABLE) instead of half-parsing. Its YAML-safety was nonetheless checked with PyYAML 6.0.3 in the port step, which is how two unescaped apostrophes in my first port were caught before the commit.
